audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty framing leaned on 'out-ranging your plan'; the real gate is a 2-second untargetable Sanguine Pool plus Transfusion sustain.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and 16s at rank 5, 2 seconds untargetable — it eats an entire Diana combo. Transfusion costs 0 mana, so chip trades never stick.
audit.corrected: EVEN 5.5/10 kept; enemyWin, cooldowns and don'ts now name the pool timer and the sustain instead of range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart read Skill/Diana/Diana/Skill/Diana/Skill/Vladimir while content win[] and the packet chart both read Diana on all seven rows.
audit.why: Every phases[].why on those rows already describes Diana winning the stage, so the sides were the stale half. Row 6's why also describes Diana diving.
audit.corrected: phases[0,3,5,6].side moved to Diana; win[] already Diana on all rows, so no cross-layer disagreement is introduced and no why needed rewriting.

audit.whatIsWrong: No statement of the two interactions that decide the matchup: Sanguine Pool's untargetability voiding a committed combo, and Moonlight refunding Lunar Rush.
audit.why: Lunar Rush has no cooldown onto a Moonlight target and 22s at rank 1 otherwise; Sanguine Pool makes him untargetable for 2 seconds, so an unmarked dash is a 22s spend into nothing.
audit.corrected: Stated in dosFull[0]/[2], dontsFull[0]/[2] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds timing was mentioned only in a report line, never in the fields that drive play.
audit.why: Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal him; extended trades and dives are decided by anti-heal timing.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal now appears in breakdown.carry, breakdown.feeding and wants.you[2].

audit.why: Real numbers make the bait-the-pool advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Pool 28s/16s, Transfusion down to 4.6s, Hemoplague flat 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED); dosFull[2].d cited a 'fifteen-second' cooldown that does not exist in his kit.
audit.why: Bodies must match their titles and quote real numbers.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Pale Cascade has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — 2 seconds untargetable that eats your whole combo, so bait it, count 28, then commit. - Transfusion costs no mana and hits 4.6s late, so chip damage never buys you the lane; Hemoplague is a flat 120s.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Crescent Strike outranges his 600 Transfusion — poke from outside it and the Moonlight mark makes Lunar Rush free.

edits.before: Q through the wave onto his chest, E the mark, three-hit string, walk — the phase trade he answers after you've left.
edits.after: Pale Cascade's third orb fattens the shield — trade while orbs are up and his Tides of Blood chip cannot out-heal your string.

edits.before: Vladimir burns Sanguine Pool on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: A Moonlight mark refunds Lunar Rush; dash unmarked and you burn 22s next to him.

edits.before: That’s Vladimir’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Unmarked E is 22s spent walking into a 2-second pool where he cannot be hit.

edits.before: Dashing onto an unmarked target with W down — Diana without the reset or the shield is a melee mage donating proximity.
edits.after: Without a mark there is no reset, and Transfusion heals him back through everything your three-hit string put on him.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling out of your combo, healing the chip back with Transfusion, and outscaling you on Crimson Pact.

edits.before: Carry through the dive — mark, dash, pull, delete; your R turns their teamfight spacing into a suggestion.
edits.after: Vladimir survives by pooling and healing — buy Grievous Wounds before you dive, then Moonfall him with the clump.

edits.before: If Vladimir opens the score, reset expectations and respect Sanguine Pool doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q arcs and stay relevant through R engage.
edits.after: If Vladimir opens the score, his Crimson Pact health-and-AP loop compounds every gold he gets — farm with Q arcs, buy Grievous Wounds early, and stay relevant by pulling clumps with Moonfall.

edits.before: Snowball your early item lead into more aggressive all-ins
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds early to cut Transfusion and Hemoplague

notes: All seven content win[] rows and the packet chart agree on Diana; four full-layer sides were stale and were moved to match, with every why on those rows already Diana-favorable so none required rewriting. tradeGood/tradeBad left alone — still somewhat generic, but Vladimir's kit gives nothing further to ground them without inventing. Whether Sanguine Pool's untargetability drops an already-applied Moonlight mark is not in Riot's text and was not asserted.
